The memory bank's latest analysis (Step 10 status) concluded that the nullptr guard at line 175 should prevent the double-free from actually executing. When ~Application() calls shutdown() at line 186, g_custom_heap will already be nullptr (set at line 178 during the first shutdown call), so the if-guard prevents re-entry.

The memory bank suggests the actual crash source is "possibly static libstdc++ objects being destroyed after custom heap cleanup" - which aligns with your Step 9 hypothesis about initializing stdlib features in user_init() before the custom heap activates.

The fix strategy from Step 9 appears sound: use user_init() (called at line 146, before g_custom_heap setup at line 149) to force initialization of static libstdc++ objects using normal malloc, preventing them from being allocated from the custom heap and later freed after heap destruction.
